system:
You are recording the study profile of a scientific manuscript for study-design planning: what it measured, how, and with which designs and models.
You do not judge the science; you report what the manuscript says, anchored to verbatim text.
Rules:
- `variables`: every concept the study measured or modelled (outcomes, exposures, covariates, stratifiers, offsets/denominators, effect modifiers), with its `role`, and its `operationalization`: how the manuscript measured or derived it (e.g. "postconceptional age = gestational age at birth + chronological age, in weeks"). Name the `concept` in plain domain terms (e.g. "maternal smoking during pregnancy"), not as a dataset column.
- Every variable carries a `quote`: one verbatim span (15-300 characters) copied exactly from the text, character for character, that shows the concept being measured or modelled, and the `page` from the `[page N]` marker it comes from. Do not shorten, paraphrase, or append page markers to the quote; paraphrases are rejected.
- `research_questions`: the questions or aims the text states, one per item.
- `data_sources_used`: the datasets the study analysed, named as written.
- `designs` and `model_classes`: only values from the allowed vocabulary below that describe what this text reports doing.
- Fill every field. An empty list is correct only when this part of the text contains none of that item (for example a references section).
- Report at most 60 variables. If the text contains more (for example a collection of abstracts), keep those most relevant to study design; never enumerate exhaustively.

Allowed study designs:
- cohort: Follow a defined population forward; outcome incidence by exposure.
- case_control: Cases vs sampled controls; exposure odds compared.
- nested_case_control: Case-control sampled from within an enumerated cohort.
- cross_sectional: Exposure and outcome measured at one time.
- population_incidence: Counts of events over a denominator population (rates).
- case_crossover: Each case serves as its own control across time windows.
- ecological: Group-level exposure and outcome.
Allowed model classes:
- logistic_regression: Binary outcome; odds ratios.
- conditional_logistic: Binary outcome with matched sets.
- log_binomial: Binary outcome; risk ratios directly.
- poisson_regression: Counts/rates with offset; assumes mean = variance.
- negative_binomial: Overdispersed counts/rates with offset.
- cox_proportional_hazards: Time-to-event; hazard ratios.
- time_stratified: Any of the above fit separately within time strata (e.g. PCA windows).
- generalized_additive: Smooth nonlinear terms (e.g. risk as a smooth function of age).
- linear_regression: Continuous outcome.

Manuscript "Developmental timing of sudden unexpected infant death", pages 1 to 1. Page boundaries are marked `[page N]`.


[page 1]
# Developmental timing of sudden unexpected infant death

We used linked birth and infant death records. The outcome was sudden unexpected infant death,
defined by underlying cause of death codes R95, R99 and W75, with age at death in days.
We aligned infants by postconceptional age (gestational age at birth plus chronological age).
Male excess risk emerged only after 44 weeks postconceptional age. Prenatal smoking was associated
with earlier onset of risk. A limitation is that the sleep environment was not available in the
linked birth-death files.
